subject: Recap: Geo & deployment follow-up — GrayBank evaluation
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Stein <emma.stein@graybank.com>; GrayBank - Architecture Team <arch-team@graybank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 13:12:00 +0000
Subject: Recap: Geo & deployment follow-up — GrayBank evaluation

Thanks again for taking the demo call this morning. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we loop legal/infra: 

Key takeaways from today's call:
- Data residency: GrayBank requires transaction PII and audit logs for EU customers to remain in EU jurisdiction. Some user metadata can cross borders for analytics, but legal wants strong controls.
- Deployment appetite: initial comfort with Hosted API for MVP EU users, but strong interest in Private VPC for EU-regulated flows and a Dedicated pool for heavy batch scoring in the US.
- APAC latency: internal product team flagged Singapore users need median p95 latency under ~120ms for interactive flows.
- Failover/routing: GrayBank asked whether we can route EU requests to EU-only endpoints and block cross-border fallback by policy; also asked about fallback behavior during region outages.
- Security/compliance: they want KMS integration (customer-managed keys), SOC2 evidence, and an initial questionnaire answered before a pilot.

Proposed next steps (action items):
1) Redwood to confirm concrete options (Hosted EU-only routing limitations, Dedicated EU reserved pool, Private VPC onboarding timeline) and send high-level cost/commit ranges — Ben to own pricing sketch.
2) Share compliance artifacts and our standard SOW draft — attaching compliance packet and a starter SOW.
3) Schedule a 60-min architecture session that includes one of our infra engineers (to discuss VPC peering, routing policies) and a security lead. Propose Thu 22 Apr or Mon 26 Apr.
4) Emma to confirm which user flows must be EU-resident vs which can be routed out of-region for analytics.

Attachments included: redwood_compliance_packet_v2.pdf, SOW-draft-GrayBank.pdf (stubs).

If that reads correctly, I'll loop in Legal (for NDA/contract timing) and Solutions (for scheduling).

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov

From: Emma Stein <emma.stein@graybank.com>

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 17:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Recap: Geo & deployment follow-up — GrayBank evaluation

Olga — thanks for the clear summary. A couple clarifications/questions from our side: 

- Residency must be strictly enforced for transaction PII and audit logs. We can't have those cross to non-EU clouds under any condition, including fallbacks. Is that possible with Hosted, or does that force us to Private?
- For Dedicated: is it feasible to have a dedicated EU pool (not shared with other tenants) that also supports our overnight scoring jobs? Estimated throughput: 80k requests/hour peak for scoring.
- APAC: our business team is worried about having people in Singapore hit EU endpoints and pay the latency tax. Can Redwood do an APAC-hosted endpoint for non-PII flows?
- Compliance packet looks good at a glance. Please also include a short note on KMS customer-managed keys and whether we can put the keys in our EU KMS.

We'd like to proceed to a short pilot if the architecture allows: 2-week pilot limited to anonymized EU transactions plus metadata-only scoring from APAC. We'll need an NDA and a SOW outline to present to procurement.

Can you have someone from Solutions (& security) join the architecture call on Thu 22 Apr at 15:00 UTC?

Best,
Emma
Emma Stein
Head of Platform Architecture, GrayBank
emma.stein@graybank.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Stein <emma.stein@graybank.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:00:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Recap: Geo & deployment follow-up — GrayBank evaluation

Hi Emma — copying Marissa (Solutions). Quick technical readout and options so you have something concrete for procurement/architecture: 

Short answers up front:
- Hosted API: We offer regionally pinned hosted endpoints (EU region) and can enforce routing policies on a per-tenant basis to prefer EU endpoints. However, the hosted product currently allows configurable fallbacks to compatible regions in case of regional outage; we can configure a strict "no-fallback" policy for PII/audit flows but that is a policy-level setting (i.e., we will not route those payloads out of EU). If your legal insists on absolute physical separation (no possibility of cross-border egress even under operational exceptions), Private VPC is the conservative path.
- Dedicated EU pool: Yes — we can provision a Dedicated capacity pool restricted to your account in the EU. It can handle 80k RPS? I think you meant 80k requests/hour; for 80k req/hour peak we recommend an n1 configuration (we'll size GPUs and concurrency). I'll include cost ranges in the estimate.
- APAC for non-PII: We can host an APAC (Singapore) hosted endpoint for metadata-only flows. For the pilot, we can route anonymized scoring traffic to SG while keeping PII processed and stored only in EU.
- KMS: We support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations. You can retain keys in your EU KMS and bind operations that require decryption to EU-only hosts where the KMS is reachable.

Notes on implementation and tradeoffs:
1) Private VPC (EU): strongest control (VPC peering, egress control, opaque to other tenants). Onboarding takes longer (~6-8 weeks typical) and has platform + infra pricing. Good for regulated workflows and procurement that needs auditable separation.
2) Dedicated (EU reserved): faster (~2-3 weeks for initial capacity), predictable unit economics, supports heavy batch windows. It still sits in Redwood's infra but isolated at pool-level. Policy enforcement for routing and KV caches is available.
3) Hosted (EU region) + strict routing: fastest to get started, lowest up-front cost. Best for workloads where legal accepts policy-enforced residency (we can provide audit logs and attestations).

Proposed immediate deliverables:
- I'll attach a one-page Dedicated cost sketch and SOW starter (GB-dedicated-estimate-draft.xlsx, SOW-draft-GrayBank.pdf).
- Marissa, can you join Thu 22 Apr 15:00 UTC architecture call? We should include our Security lead (SOC evidence and KMS flows).
- Olga, I'll follow up with a concrete pilot plan that describes data subsets, anonymization approach, and acceptance criteria.

I'll also note that for strict "no-cross-border under any circumstance" requirements, Private VPC/Air-gapped on-prem is the only option that fully eliminates egress risk. Otherwise, Hosted with no-fallback policy plus dedicated EU pool gives strong practical guarantees with faster time-to-value.

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Attachments: GB-dedicated-estimate-draft.xlsx, SOW-draft-GrayBank.pdf
